episodes.210347: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northeast Illinois during the afternoon and evening of March 15th producing heavy rain and localized flooding as well as localized wind damage.
episodes.210394: From March 12th through March 14th of 2026, a large and powerful kona storm setup over the northern central Pacific, and brought numerous impacts across the state. This low was supported by a broad and potent upper level trough that lingered for many days. Impacts included flash flooding, wind damage, large surf, and strong thunderstorms.
episodes.210473: A deepening surface low pressure system was centered over Illinois and an attendant cold front extended south-southwestward sweeping from west to east across Arkansas during the afternoon and evening hours of March 15, 2026. Multiple severe thunderstorms developed in a well-defined warm sector positioned across the state where storms matured and quickly became severe producing large hail, damaging wind gusts, and tornadoes.
episodes.210649: A line of severe storms moved across SE Arkansas during the evening hours of March 15 2026. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts that downed trees and powerlines. Some of these storms produced hail.
episodes.210651: A line of severe storms moved across MS during the afternoon/evening hours of March 15 2026. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts that downed trees and powerlines. Some of these storms produced hail.
episodes.210751: A line of thunderstorms moved across southern Missouri during the afternoon and evening of March 15th. Several tornadoes occurred within this line of storms.
episodes.210818: Severe thunderstorms pushed through southeast Texas, producing damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.211084: Strong thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon of the 15th, as an upper level disturbance and associated cold front approached the region. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to nickel size.
episodes.211591: A potent weather system tracked over the Midwest on March 15, initially bringing widespread rain, thunderstorms, and even hail to the size of ping pong balls to Johnson County.
episodes.211671: A powerful blizzard tracked through the Upper Great Lakes, bringing widespread high winds with hurricane force gusts observed on the Bay of Green Bay.
episodes.211829: A strong low pressure system (987 mb) moved across Illinois during the afternoon of Sunday, March 15, 2026. The environment was characterized by high shear and weak instability. A line of storms swept across the state, producing scattered wind damage and eight tornadoes within the NWS Central Illinois coverage area.  The tornadoes occurred southeast of the I-72 corridor and all were rated EF-0 or EF-1. No injuries occurred.
episodes.211837: A strong low pressure system was near Kansas City, Missouri on the morning of Sunday, March 15th...with a warm front extending eastward into Illinois. As this warm front lifted northward across the region, scattered strong thunderstorms developed, some of which produced isolated hail up to nickel-sized in Sangamon and Cass counties.
episodes.211958: Strong low pressure (991 millibars) moving across the Upper Midwest lifted a warm front northward into the Altamaha River in southeast Georgia. Deeper moisture surged northward into northern Florida in the wake of the warm frontal passage. This combined with a warm and unstable air mass resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developing in the afternoon into evening along the inland moving sea breezes mainly south of the I-10 corridor. Cool mid-level temperatures, steep lapse rates and ML CAPE values in excess of 2,000 j/kg caused strong storms to briefly severe to develop in the late afternoon into the evening hours. The Storm Prediction Center had a Marginal (level 1 out of 5) Risk for severe thunderstorm development across the area.
episodes.212008: A negatively tilted upper-level trough began to deepen as it moved from the northern Rockies into the Middle Mississippi Valley on Sunday afternoon, driving a potent cold front eastward. Mid-level heights also began to fall Sunday afternoon as impressive kinematics overspread the region. Moderately steep mid-level lapse rates greater than 7 C/km, along with SBCAPE values of 750-1200 J/kg and storm relative helicity values upwards of 300 m2/s2 developed ahead of the cold front. An impressive line of storms formed along and ahead of the cold front, producing a half dozen weak tornadoes, 75+ mph wind gusts, and large hail across the Mid-South.

episodes.212052: During the afternoon of March 15th, a QLCS moved into eastern Missouri. Stronger segments of the QLCS produced wind damage to structures and trees along its length from Lincoln County and south into Madison County.
episodes.212066: During the afternoon and evening of March 15th, a QLCS moved through southern and south-central Illinois. Stronger segments of the QLCS produced wind damage across the region. The QLCS ended up producing 8 tornadoes while it passed through the region.
episodes.212124: Rapid thunderstorm initiation developed during the afternoon on March 15th as strong ascent occurred when a cold front interacted with a plume of returning surface moisture. Modest surface dew points in the lower to middle 60s amid steep mid-level lapse rates supported 1000-2000 J/kg of MUCAPE. 50+ knots of deep-layer shear also favored storm organization with a mixed mode of supercells and line segments. The surging nature of the front promoted rapid upscale growth into a QLCS before spreading eastward across the Red River Valley and into the Ark-La-Tex region. Strong low and mid-level shear between 200-300 m2/s2 supported embedded supercells, along with QLCS wind gusts. As a result, a 63 mph wind gust was recorded at the Idabel Mesonet site.

A Kealakekua resident reported flood waters coming down a hill and flooding his property, destroying the flooring and forcing his family to evacuate. His neighbors were reportedly hit harder; his neighbor's farm's water supply was taken offline and the flood waters broke up the asphalt on his driveway and opened many cracks. The County reportedly responded to 25 to 30 calls to save people���s lives when heavy rain bands hit Ka���u and South Kona. Between the Ka���u and South Kona Districts, 18 to 20 people were rescued. Other residents reported massive potholes, broken up asphalt, and boulders along with flooding impacting homes. Fifteen dead goats were reportedly found washed up or floating in Kawaihae harbor.

The tornado then travelled northeast, causing minor damage to the roofs of a few structures before directly hitting Mount Olive. In Mount Olive, the tornado damaged mostly trees, but the roof of a business was impacted as well. The tornado weakened as it exited town and approached Montgomery County.

The tornado entered Randolph County where it damaged mostly trees along its northeastern path. On Ritchfield Road southeast of Red Bud, the tornado did damage the roofs of a few farm outbuildings. The most substantial damage happened on South Prairie Road north of Prairie where the tornado ripped off a substantial portion of a church's roof. It dissipated shortly after just north of Grigg.

A tornado touched down near Niemanville Trail and trekked northeast, producing mostly tree damage in its path. At its strongest the tornado was able to produce minor damage to farm outbuildings and break wooden power poles. The tornado dissipated just east of East 8th Road.

This tornado began along County Road 547 where it damaged several power poles. The tornado continued towards the northeast over mostly farmland along County Road 534. It then moved into the town of Minturn where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. Additionally, a few mobile homes sustained roof damage. The tornado then crossed over Interstate 67 and Narrow Gauge Road where more trees were uprooted. As it continued to the northeast, it tracked over more farmland before causing minor roof damage to a barn off County Road 701. The tornado continued toward County Road 705 where it downed more trees and power poles before dissipating. This tornado was rated EF1 with estimated maximum winds of 105 mph.
A large tree was uprooted.
Multiple mobile homes had roofs completely torn off and several power poles fell in Minturn.
Multiple power poles fell in the vicinity of Sedgwick.

New Athens took a direct hit from this tornado. It touched down near Julia Street where it busted the windows of a local shop and damaged the roof of a warehouse building. The tornado pathed east-northeast through town, damaging, to varying extent, multiple roofs on Lela Drive. The tornado then weakened, causing less and weaker damage before dissipating just east of the Canadian National Railway.

A brief tornado touched down on the Hillsboro Country Club where it produced minor damage to a home. The tornado then travelled northeast where it damaged trees, an outbuilding, and electrical poles. The tornado dissipated just north of White Ave west of Irving.

A tornado touched down near Irving Road and North 17th Ave where it blew over a farm auger and lofted debris nearly a half mile to the southwest. The tornado then hit Witt directly where it lofted a carport and damaged multiple roofs and trees in town. The tornado tracked along State Route 16 into Coalton where it nearly completely removed the roof of a mobile home. From there, it turned nearly due north and entered the northwest portion of Nokomis. Although most of the damage done was to trees, the tornado did blow over an outdoor football scoreboard and ripped off portions of the local high school's roof.
Nickel size hail reported near Caddo Lake Dam.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree south of Coffeen. This tree blocked a road.
A report from social media showed a destroyed carport caused by thunderstorm winds.

A tornado began just south of Highway 412, damaging a grain bin and snapping a few trees along County Road 300. The tornado then caused damage to a camper along County Road 208. This tornado continued east-northeast and damaged an outbuilding on County Road 205 and caused tree damage at the intersection of County Road 205 and 214. This tornado resulted in EF-0 damage with 85 mph winds. The tornado lifted east of County Road 214.

This tornado began in an isolated patch of trees before moving into an open field. This tornado remained in an open field through its duration, causing no damage. Numerous trained spotters observed and recorded this tornado. NWS survey team inspected the area and found no damage, thus rating the tornado EFU.

This tornado started along Highway 34 W and damaged the roof of a metal outbuilding and the roof of a residence. Some damage to tree branches in this area was also noted. The tornado moved eastward towards Greene Road 125, where additional tree damage occurred along with minor damage to a barn. This tornado was rated EF-0 with 80 mph winds. The tornado lifted in a wooded area near Greene Road 125.
Straight-line winds knocked down numerous large branches and removed shingles from a house on CR 224.

This tornado began on the east side of Nokomis in Montgomery County, producing widespread tree damage. The tornado continued northeast, crossing into Christian County north-northwest of the town of Ohlman. The tornado continued northeast, impacting Rosamond and producing roof and tree damage. It then curved east into Pana where it uprooted and snapped several large trees before dissipating. The tornado produced EF-1 damage in both counties, and it lasted a total of 14 minutes, spanning 13.6 miles.

The tornado continued northeast, causing minor roof damage to a residence near the intersection of Greene Roads 151 and 142. A small barn was also destroyed off Greene Road 142 near Highway 135. The tornado crossed Highway 135 and damaged a barn just south of Highway 34 E. This damage was consistent with a 90 mph EF1 tornado. The tornado lifted in a wooded area north of Highway 34 E.
Trees downed in Nacogdoches with sporadic downed trees also reported throughout Nacogdoches County.
The rear flank downdraft associated with the EF-1 tornado that struck Lafe, Arkansas uprooted trees and caused roof damage to a mobile home south of the tornado track.

The tornado continued through Assumption, producing more tree damage and removing roofing material from a downtown building. The tornado damage a few more trees northeast of town before dissipating prior to reaching Highway 51. The tornado was rated EF-1, and was in progress for just two minutes.

The tornado continued northeast, causing minor roof damage to a residence near the intersection of County Roads 420 and 418. In addition, roof uplift occurred to a metal outbuilding on the property. Damage was consistent with a 90 mph EF1 tornado. The tornado lifted shortly after crossing County Road 418.
Quarter size hail reported in the Tiburon neighborhood in North Bossier City.
Nickel size hail reported at the Bossier Parish 911 Center in North Bossier City.

Straight line winds knocked down a tree, a utility pole, and caused outbuilding damage on Rogers Chapel Road. A tree was uprooted, and an outbuilding was damaged on CR 910. Some shingles were ripped off a house on CR 910.
An outbuilding was destroyed, and a second one was partially damaged near the intersection of South Dodd Street and West 13th Street. Several trees were also downed.

Half dollar size hail reported just north of Logansport.

This tornado began two miles west of Lovington along County Road 700 E and progressed to the northeast. Along its path, the tornado snapped large tree branches and uprooted one tree. It also produced roof damage to a home and outbuilding. Near the end of its path, the tornado snapped a power pole along County Road 2500 N, and it eventually dissipated near Lanton or about three miles north of Lovington. It was rated EF-1 and was in progress for six minutes.
Half dollar size hail reported in the Chireno community.
A trained spotter estimated winds of 50 to 60 mph and shared a video of the conditions at their location.

A tornado touched down just east of Baird between County Roads 316 and 320 overturning multiple center pivots. The tornado continued into the town of Clarkton, causing roof damage to a state school, convenience store, and multiple homes along Page Street just south of W Highway 162. Additional damage was noted to an outbuilding south of E Highway 162, with debris spreading into a nearby field. The tornado lifted just before the town of Gideon.
Penny-sized hail fell near the town of St. Charles.
Damage to a porch and garage door. A fence and large tree branches were knocked down.
Roof damage and powerlines downed at the intersection of Beauchamp Street and West Lake Street.
Quarter size hail fell near Fountain Hill.
Missouri mesonet site reported 59 mph wind gust.
Half-dollar sized hail fell in the town of Jerome.
Multiple trees downed in Dixie Inn.
Hail up to the size of golf balls fell.
A six-foot tall wooden fence had several fence lengths blown down by thunderstorm wind gusts.

The tornado began about two miles southeast of Arthur near N County Road 100 E, producing damage to trees and outbuildings and strewing the debris across fields to the northeast. The tornado turned east, producing additional tree and outbuilding damage along E County Road 300 N. The tornado then turned sharply north, producing similar tree and outbuilding damage before dissipating prior to reaching Highway 133. The tornado was rated EF-0, and was in progress for three minutes.
Quarter to ping pong ball size reported in the Goodwin community southwest of San Augustine.
Multiple trees downed in Heflin.
